default_port_notes.9009: Cortex HTTP API (single-binary/monolithic default) — distributor push + querier read live here
default_port_notes.8080: Common override / per-component HTTP on microservices deployments

auth_config_env: auth_enabled: true (default) -> every read/write request MUST carry X-Scope-OrgID or it is rejected with a 401/'no org id'
auth_enabled: false -> all requests forced to tenant 'fake' (single-tenant, still no real auth)
Real auth is delegated to an upstream gateway/proxy — Cortex itself only does tenant routing on the header
misconfig_patterns: X-Scope-OrgID is identity, NOT a secret — any client that knows/guesses a tenant ID reads that tenant's series (no per-tenant credential)
auth_enabled:false collapses everything to tenant 'fake' — a single unauth header-less read returns ALL data
/distributor/all_user_stats enumerates EVERY tenant ID + ingestion rate — the Cortex-unique multi-tenant disclosure (leaks the full customer/tenant list)
/ingester/ring and /distributor/ha_tracker expose ring membership / node IPs
/config returns the full running Cortex config (object-store creds, limits)
/api/v1/push accepts remote-write — unauth metric injection into a named tenant if reachable

active_probe.false_positive_check: POSITIVE Cortex discriminator: /distributor/all_user_stats and /ingester/ring are Cortex-native admin routes that Prometheus, VM, Thanos and Mimir do NOT serve (Mimir RENAMED these and dropped the /distributor/all_user_stats path — see mimir.json). On a bare /api/v1/query with no X-Scope-OrgID, Cortex returns the 'no org id' / 401 tenant error (SHARED tell with Mimir — disambiguate via the admin route + the /api/prom path prefix Cortex keeps for back-compat). buildinfo: Cortex returns Prometheus-compat build fields; NOT VM's empty {}.

shodan_dorks.tenant_error: (Censys — 'no org id' / 401 is a JSON/body-on-non-200 response the Shodan web UI under-indexes; route to Censys http body)

deployment_tells: Dual path prefixes: Cortex serves both /api/prom/* (legacy) AND /prometheus/* AND bare /api/v1/* — the /api/prom/ prefix is a back-compat tell absent in Prometheus/VM
/services route lists the dskit module lifecycle (distributor/ingester/querier/store-gateway) — Cortex/Mimir family tell
pivot_paths: GET /distributor/all_user_stats -> full tenant ID roster + per-tenant ingestion rate -> customer enumeration
GET /ingester/ring -> ring node membership + internal IPs -> backend topology
GET /config -> running config -> object-store credentials + limits
GET /prometheus/api/v1/query with a discovered X-Scope-OrgID -> that tenant's stored series (read surface)
POST /api/v1/push with X-Scope-OrgID -> unauth metric injection (write surface — SEPARATE severity)
vulnerabilities: Design choice (NOT a CVE): X-Scope-OrgID is tenant identity, not authentication; multi-tenant isolation depends entirely on an upstream gateway that operators often omit
auth_enabled:false -> single 'fake' tenant collapse is a documented foot-gun, not a CVE
CVE churn in Cortex is largely Go-stdlib/dependency class (image-level), not application-logic
auth_default_thesis: TENANT-IDENTITY-DEFAULT (not auth-off, not auth-on). Cortex differs from VM/Prometheus/Thanos: requests without X-Scope-OrgID are rejected ('no org id'). But the header is identity, not a credential — there is no per-tenant secret in Cortex itself. So a population dork over /api/v1/query OVER-COUNTS: many Cortex hosts answer the tenant error (looks 'protected') yet leak the entire tenant list via /distributor/all_user_stats and serve any tenant's data to anyone supplying the (often guessable: 'fake','anonymous','1','demo') org ID. The auth-on-default thesis must be scored at the TENANT-ENUMERATION layer, not the bare-query layer, for this platform.
research_questions: What share of exposed Cortex serve /distributor/all_user_stats unauthenticated (full tenant roster leak)?
How often is auth_enabled:false (single 'fake' tenant -> bare unauth read)?
Do common org IDs (fake/anonymous/1/demo) read real data on auth_enabled:true hosts?
Does /config leak object-store credentials at population scale?
